newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish paedophile priest gets 12-year jail sentence.
newsitem.headline: Irish paedophile priest gets 12-year jail sentence.

text.p: A paedophile Roman Catholic priest whose crimes helped topple an Irish government was jailed for 12 years on Friday.
Brendan Smyth, 71, admitted a 36-year litany of sex offences against 20 children in the Republic of Ireland.
Judge Cyril Kelly said the case, involving 74 counts of indecent and sexual assaults, was one of the most serious ever dealt with by his Dublin court.
One of his victims shouted "rot in hell, Smyth," as the priest was led from the court.
Smyth, a former member of the Norbertine Order, was extradited from British-ruled Northern Ireland in March after serving four years for abusing children there.
The judge took account of Smyth's guilty pleas but said he feared he would seriously abuse children again.
Revelations of Smyth's activities shook Ireland's Roman Catholic Church and the nation's four million devout churchgoers.
It was the first of several sex abuse cases involving clerics that deepened public outrage and led church authorities to draw up guidelines for dealing with the problem.
A 1994 furore about a seven-month Irish delay in processing Smyth's extradition to Northern Ireland damaged the then government of Albert Reynolds.
His adminstration later collapsed in a row over high-level legal appointments.
The Norbertine Order in a statement on Friday expressed sorrow and regret for what it acknowledged as "a further series of grave offences against children".
It said it had referred the paedophile for expert treatment several times but it had become aware as the years passed that he was resisting prescribed treatment.
In court last Tuesday Smyth apologised to his victims saying the offences were sins against God.

"While the great majority of these cases occurred 20 to 30 years ago, I recognise them all for what they were - sins against God, offences against individual persons and offences against the laws of the state," he said in a statement read out to the Dublin Circuit Criminal Court.
